newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Kwik Save reviews after dire year.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Kwik Save reviews after dire year.

text.p: British low price supermarket retailer Kwik Save, pincered between discounters and leading supermarkets, should see year profits slump when it reports on November 7 and could cut its dividend, analysts said.

The company, in which Hong Kong's Dairy Farm holds a 29.4 percent stake, is also expected to announce results of a strategic review aimed at halting its decline, which could carry exceptional charges anywhere between 60-100 million stg.

"Obviously, this year has been a disaster in profit terms. Kwik Save has a one-track marketing strategy -- price -- at a time when that is not particularly in vogue," said one sector analyst who asked not to be identified.

Analysts are expecting pretax, pre-exceptional profits to slump to 82.0 to 90.0 million stg from 125.5 million stg a year ago, while best estimates see the dividend maintained at 20 pence per share with some seeing a cut to around 15 pence.

As the big four supermarkets have moved away from price to stress value and quality, fierce competition has emerged at the bottom end of the market among discounters and low-price Kwik Save has been caught in the middle, analysts said.

It warned at half year results in May that sales were flat with price inflation at around one percent, saying that gross margins would be cut in the second half from a year ago after a 0.2 percent slip in the first half.
"If Kwik Save did not exist, you would not invent it," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
The company has undertaken a strategic review to address its problems and analysts suggested it might close between 100-300 unprofitable stores and even consider a change of name.
There could be hefty provisions around this which might take Kwik Save into a pretax, post-exceptional loss, they added.
"I would like to see Kwik Save wipe the slate clean at this stage, the question is whether they can," said the sector analyst.

Analysts said that Kwik Save's locations, many of which are in neighbourhoods not well served by market leaders Tesco, J. Sainsbury, ASDA and Safeway, which might allow it a niche as a local retailer.
But others remained sceptical, suggesting that while price remained an attraction for only a minority of supermarket shoppers, Kwik Save would continue to be squeezed.
"At some stage the way forward for Kwik Save will be through a takeover, as part of a larger group," the sector analyst said.
But even that could be a long way off as the chain does not look attractive to a predator at this point, analysts said.
Hong Kong's Dairy Farm holds a 29.4 percent stake in Kwik Save but has not made clear whether it would want to increase or decrease this position.
"I think Dairy Farm would be quite glad to get rid of that stake but there does not seem to be an obvious buyer," the analyst said.
